G: I’m working on an experiment for the science
fair. This is the third time I’ve failed!
B: Don’t get discouraged! Have you ever heard of
the 147/805 rule? It can encourage you to keep
trying after you fail.
G: I’ve never heard of it. Can you tell me what it
is? __________________________________________________
B: Sure. Each number represents the number of
times a great scientist failed before making a
great scientific achievement. 147 is the number
of
times
Thomas
Edison
failed
before
he
invented the light bulb.
G: Wow! That’s a lot!
B: Well, don’t be too surprised yet. The Wright
brothers tried 805 times before they finally had
success flying an airplane. In short, inventors
have achieved great things after many failures.
G: I didn’t know those great inventors went through
so much trial and error. Now I’m not afraid to
try again and again!

I'd find it hard to believe it.
I’d be very interested to know.
I'd love to hear more about it.
I'd like to know more about it.
solution: 과학 박람회를 위한 실험에서 세 번째 실패해 기분이 좋지 않은 유미에게 소년이 낙담하지 말라고 말하며 147/805 규칙이 계 속 도전하는 데 도움이 될 것이라고 했고, 이에 대해 유미가 들 어본 적이 없다고 답하며 그것에 대해 말해달라고 요청했으며, 이어서 소년이 그것은 위대한 과학자들이 과학적 업적을 이루 기까지 실패한 횟수를 나타낸다고 상세히 설명해 주고 있으므 로, 소년이 언급한 147/805에 대해 유미가 궁금증이나 호기심 을 보인 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 어떤 놀라운 사실에 대해 알게 된 뒤 그것이 믿기 어려울 것이라고 반응하는 표현인 ❷ ‘나는 그것을 믿기 어려울 것 같아.’는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.

body:
In Alberta, Canada, there were some “aurora
chasers” who formed an informal group online.
They would leave their homes at night and try to
get exceptional photographs of auroras. Then they
would share them with the rest of the group.
In the summer of 2014, the group members
__________________________________. There were unusual
ribbons of green and purple light, some of which
seemed to stretch for thousands of kilometers.
Sometimes they lasted for just a few minutes, while
other times they remained in the sky for a whole
hour. They were similar in appearance to auroras,
yet they possessed some notably different features.
Unsure of what they were, the group decided to
name the phenomenon “Steve,” based on a scene
from an animated movie where some characters
give that name to an unfamiliar object.

body:
One evening after work, Schawinski met a friend
named Chris Lintott and complained about the
situation. Lintott suggested that he turn to the
Internet to ask other people for help. Eventually,
the two men ended up launching a crowdsourced
online project known as Galaxy Zoo. The website
was kept as (A)____________ as possible, with a very
basic design and an easy-to-use interface. This
allowed those who wanted to participate to get
started quickly. New visitors were greeted with a
brief tutorial that explained the project. Then they
were shown an image of a galaxy and asked to
click buttons that described its features. Is the
galaxy smooth and rounded? Is its shape an oval or
a spiral? After completion of the tutorial and a little
bit of practice, the participants were able to classify
galaxies effectively.
It was online media that helped spread the word
about
Galaxy
Zoo,
bringing
more
and
more
participants to the website. Shortly after the website
was launched, nearly 70,000 classifications were
being made per hour. In a year and a half, more
than 80,000 individuals participated, and they made
more than 75 million classifications. If it had not
been for those participants, Schawinski couldn’t
have classified that many images. In fact, it would
have taken him decades on his own.
More than 15 years have passed since the project
first began in 2007. Galaxy Zoo has now grown into
Zooniverse, which is one of the most popular
platforms on the Internet for (B)____________ people
who want to participate in science projects. It is
more active than ever before, with about 2 million
registered users worldwide. It now offers a wide
range of projects in astronomy, biology, physics,
and more. If you want to get involved, you should
definitely check it out!

(A)
(B)
choices: secureprivileged
complexordinary

solution: (A) 매우 기본적인 디자인과 사용하기 쉬운 인터페이스를 가졌 으며, 참여하기를 원하는 사람들이 빠르게 시작할 수 있게 했 다는 설명이 이어지므로, 웹사이트가 최대한 단순하게 유지되 었다는 흐름이 되는 simple(간단한, 단순한)이 적절하다. (B) 대중을 참여시키는(=크라우드소싱) 온라인 프로젝트인 Galaxy Zoo의 신규 방문자들은 은하수의 분류 전에 간단한 사 용 지침의 완료와 약간의 연습을 거쳤다고 했으며, 글의 마지 막에 참여하고 싶다면 확인해 보라고 권유하고 있는 것으로 보아, 특별한 전문 지식이나 기술이 없이도 누구나 참여 가능 하다는 것을 알 수 있다. 따라서 Galaxy Zoo가 Zooniverse로 성장하여 이제는 과학 프로젝트에 참여하고 싶어 하는 일반인 들을 위한 인기 있는 플랫폼 중 하나라는 흐름이 되는 ordinary(평범한, 보통의)가 적절하다.

They began the process of developing their
vaccine by gathering samples of the bacteria that
cause whooping cough. To support them, local
doctors and nurses provided “cough plates” from
their patients. The patients coughed onto a petri
dish*, which was then put into an incubator. This
allowed the bacteria to grow into colonies ⓐwhere
Kendrick and Eldering could analyze. When they
collected samples on their own, they would go to
the homes of sick children. Each time, they were
reminded once again of the dreadful suffering
ⓑcaused by the disease. The sight of these
innocent young victims ⓒcoughed and struggled to
breathe was a powerful reminder of the urgent
need for an effective vaccine.

was safe. From 1934 to 1935, they conducted their
first field test with 1,592 children. In the group of

One evening in late November 1932, a bitterly

expand their research and run more tests with

their
battle
against
whooping
cough.
Eleanor
Roosevelt, whose husband suffered from polio*, was
interested in fighting infectious diseases. She spent
time with the women and came to realize the
enormous importance of their work. With her help,

funding to conduct a large-scale trial.

body:
A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a
psychology
professor
at
Cornell
University,
reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t
spend your money on things. We assume that the
happiness we get from buying something will last
as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The
trouble with things is that the happiness they
provide fades quickly. There are three critical
reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. What once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
get used to a new possession, we look for an even
better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to
compare themselves with others. We buy a new car
and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better
one, and there’s always someone with a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we
are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves
than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really
like your material stuff. You can even think that
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On
the other hand, your experiences really are part of
you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Role of Social Values in Shaping One‘s Identity
The Psychological Drive Behind the Pursuit ofMaterial Wealth
Experiences Over Possessions: The Key to LastingHappiness
Why People Seek Greater Happiness Through NewLife Experiences
The Pursuit of Happiness: Balancing MaterialWealth and Personal Fulfillment
solution: 물건이 주는 행복은 익숙해짐, 더 높은 기준, 다른 사람과의 비 교로 인해 빨리 사라지는 반면, 경험은 우리의 정체성의 일부 가 되어 물건보다 오래 지속되는 행복을 가져다준다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ❸ ‘소유보다 경험: 지속적인 행복의 열쇠’가 알맞다.

A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a psychology professor at Cornell University, ⓐreached
a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t spend your
money on things. We assume that the happiness
we get from buying something will (A)last as long
as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The trouble with
things is that the happiness they provide ⓑfading
quickly. There are three critical reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. ⓒThat once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep (B)lowering the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
ⓓget used to a new possession, we look for an
even better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans
ⓔto compare themselves with others. We buy a
new car and are (C)thrilled with it until a friend
buys a better one, and there’s always someone with
a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we are
the (D)accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we ⓕhave been.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves than
our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really
like your material stuff. You can even think  ⓖthat
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain (E)separate from you.
On the other hand, your experiences really are part
of you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

~하든지‘라는 뜻으로 양 보의 부사절을 이끌 때, no matter who를 사용해 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 오답 ⓐ ‘전치사+추상명사(구)’는 부사(구)로 전환 가능하므로 ‘with+추상명사구’ 형태로 ‘매우 쉽게’라는 의미를 가지는 with great ease를 동일한 의미의 부사구 very easily로 전 환한 것은 알맞다. ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에 쓰인 빅데이터 알고리즘 기술을 적용하여 기업이 고객들의 요구, 기호, 소비 패턴들을 확인하고 사람들은 다양한 선택과 맞춤화를 환영하며 결과적으로 그들의 만족이 높아진다는 부연 설명이 이어지므로, 기업이 고 객들 개인의 선호에 맞춘 개별화된 제품이나 서비스를 제공할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ④ ‘기업들이 고객들에게 맞춤형 제품과 서비스를 제공 하는 것을 쉽게 만든다’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 기업들이 정기적인 디지털 상호작용을 통해 고객들 과 더 긴밀한 관계를 유지하도록 돕는다 ② 기업들이 고객들에게 디지털 콘텐츠에 대한 더 편리 한 접근을 제공하는 것을 가능하게 만든다 ③ 기업들이 고객들에게 제품과 서비스를 전달하는 비 용을 줄이는 것을 허용한다 ⑤ 기업들이 고객들의 개별적인 선호를 이해할 필요가 없게 만든다 9) are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience : • 주어 subscription services가 ‘접근 가능하게 만들어지는’ 대상이므로, 5형식 구문인 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(형용 사(구))(~를 …하게[…한 상태로] 만들다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘be made+형용사(구)(~가 …하게[…한 상태로] 만들어지다)’를 활용한다. 주어가 복수명사구이므로 복수형 be동사로 수일 치한 수동태 are made와 형용사구 easily accessible을 쓴 뒤, ‘by+명사구’인 by online platforms가 이어지도록 한다. • 콤마(,) 뒤에 <조건>에 따라 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 사용하되, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 ‘증진시키는’ 원인이므로, enhance를 능동을 나타내 는 현재분사 enhancing으로 변형하고 이어서 목적어인 명 사구 consumers’ convenience를 써서 완성한다. 10) ②: Furthermore(게다가)로 시작하여 소비자들이 유연성과 편의성을 높이 평가한다고 말한 뒤 이러한 소비자의 성향에 따라 구독 모델들이 유연성을 갖추고 소비자의 편의를 증진시킨다는 점을 설명하고 있으므로, 앞에서 도 현대 소비자들이 가치를 두는 점과 그에 따른 구독 모델의 특성을 다루었음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 글의 바 로 앞에 왔을 내용으로 ② ‘구독 모델이 충족하는 최근 소비자의 선호도와 요구’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 소비자들이 과거에 선호했던 제품과 서비스의 특징 ③ 구독 모델의 부정적인 영향과 그것들을 극복하는 방법 ④ 구독 기반 서비스와 제품에 관한 소비자 불만 ⑤ 구독 기반 소비의 하락하는 인기 11) ②: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다. ⓑ fading → fades (is 뒤 명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 명사절에서 주어 the happiness they provide에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 주어의 핵심이 단수명사구 the happiness이므로, fading을 단수동사로 수일치한 fades 로 고친다.) ⓒ That → What (뒤에 이어진 불완전한 절 ‘once seemed ~ exciting’을 이끌어 문장의 동사 becomes에 대한 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, That을 선행사를 포함해 ‘~하는 것’의 의미를 나타내는 관계대명사 What으로 고친다.) ⓕ have been → have been to (we 이하는 목적격 관 계대명사 that 또는 which가 생략되고 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절의 형태로 앞의 명사구 the places를 수식 하는 관계사절이 되어야 하므로, 선행사인 the places를 의미상 목적어로 취할 수 있는 전치사를 넣어 have been to로 고친다.) 본문변형 we’ve been to → we have been to 오답 ⓐ 주어 A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 Thomas Gilovich에 대한 동격 명사구 a psychology professor at Cornell University 뒤에 문장의 동사가 올 자리이며, reach는 ‘~ 에 이르다’라는 뜻의 타동사로 쓰이며 뒤에 목적어로 명 사구 a powerful and clear conclusion이 이어져 있으므 로, 흐름상 과거시제이자 능동태로 쓴 reached는 알맞다. ⓔ ’~을 자극해서 …하다‘라는 뜻으로 ’stimulate+목적어 +목적격보어(to부정사)‘를 쓸 수 있으므로, stimulate와 목적어 humans 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to compare는 알맞다. 12) ②: (B) lowering(낮추는) → raising(올리는) 13) ⑤: 물질적 소유는 익숙해짐, 높아지는 기대, 타인과의 비교 로 인해 지속적인 행복을 주기 어렵지만, 경험은 우리 의 정체성의 일부가 되어 더 오래 지속되는 행복을 가 져다준다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 목적으로 ⑤ ‘경험이 물질적 소유보다 왜 더 지속적인 행복을 가져 다주는지를 설명하기 위해’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 현대 사회에서 소비 습관이 어떻게 발전해 왔는지를 탐구하기 위해 ② 소비와 사회적 지위 간의 관계를 분석하기 위해 ③ 경험의 질이 행복의 수준에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 를 알아보기 위해 ④ 사람들의 소유물에 대한 애착 이면의 심리적 요인들 을 살펴보기 위해 14) ③: 구독 경제가 초래할 수 있는 환경 오염 문제와 이러한 문제를 줄이기 위한 방법을 설명한 뒤, 구독 서비스들 의 잠재적 제한점들에도 불구하고 더욱 많은 기업들이 구독 경제를 채택하고 있으며 미래에 더 많은 구독 서 비스들이 지속적으로 제공될 것이라는 점과 그에 따라 더욱 현명한 소비자가 되어야 할 필요성을 다루는 흐름 이므로, 구독 경제의 부정적 측면을 언급하는 (C) ‘그러 나 구독 경제는 소액의 반복적인 결제가 점차 누적될 수 있기 때문에 소비자들이 자신들의 지출을 파악하기 어렵게 만들 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다. 15) ①: 구독 경제는 다양한 범위의 구독 선택을 제공하여 개인 들이 자신들의 선호와 관심에 기초하여 경험을 개별화 할 수 있게 해 준다는 내용이 이어지므로, 소비자들이 개인 맞춤형 경험을 선호한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ① ‘다양성과 맞춤화에 가치를 둔다’가 알맞다. 오답 ② 안정성과 표준화를 우선시한다 ③ 디지털 서비스로부터의 독립을 추구한다 ④ 편리성과 접근성을 강조한다 ⑤ 더 많은 사회적 상호작용과 유대감을 추구한다 16) To come to the point, consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions : • 사례로 제시된 화장품 구독 서비스는 소비자의 현재 피 부 상태를 철저하게 분석하고 개개인의 고유한 피부 고 민을 해결하기 위해 만들어진 화장품 제조 및 전문적 추 천을 제공한다고 했으므로, 이처럼 소비자들이 획일적인 제품 대신 각자의 필요와 요구에 맞춘 개별적 경험을 얻 는다고 정리 요약하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 주어 진 제시어를 사용해 ‘요점을 말하자면, 소비자들은 그들 개인의 피부 조건을 우선시하는 개별화된 경험을 얻는다’ 라는 뜻이 되도록 영작한다. • <조건>에 따라 독립부정사구를 주절 앞에 콤마(,)와 함 께 쓰되, 제시어를 사용해 ‘요점을 말하자면’이라는 뜻으 로 To come to the point를 쓴다. • 주절의 주어로 consumers, 동사로 receive, 목적어로 a personalized experience를 쓴다. 이어서 명사구 a personalized experience를 수식하는 관계사절을 주격 관 계대명사 that을 사용해 ‘that+주어가 없는 불완전한 절’ 의 형태로 쓴다. 이때, that 뒤에는 단수명사구인 선행사 에 수일치한 단수동사 prioritizes를 쓰고, 목적어로 their individual skin conditions를 써서 완성한다. 17) ⑤: 화장품 구독 서비스는 소비자의 현재 피부 상태와 개별 적인 피부 고민을 철저하게 분석하고, 이에 맞는 맞춤 형 화장품과 전문적인 추천을 제공한다고 언급하고 있 으나, 개별 소비자들의 구체적인 피부 고민과 관련된 내용은 다루고 있지 않으므로, ⑤ ‘화장품 구독 서비스 는 무슨 종류의 피부 고민을 가장 많이 다루는가?’에는 답할 수 없다. 오답 ① 왜 소비자들은 구독 경제를 매력적이라고 생각하는가? (→ 소유할 필요 없이 서비스나 콘텐츠에 접근할 수 있 기 때문이다.) ② 의류 구독 서비스는 소비자들에게 무슨 편의를 제공 하는가? (→ 서랍을 채우지 않고도(개인적으로 옷을 소 유하지 않고도) 다양한 의류 스타일을 탐색할 수 있게 한다.) ③ 개인들은 자신의 경험을 개별화할 때 무엇을 고려할 수 있는가? (→ 그들 자신의 선호와 관심을 고려할 수 있다.) ④ 무엇이 구독 경제를 젊은 세대 사이에서 인기 있게 만드는가? (→ 자신의 선호와 관심에 기초해 경험을 개 별화할 수 있게 하는 구독 경제의 측면은 젊은 세대가 자신의 고유함을 표현하고 개별적 취향에 부합하는 가 치 있는 콘텐츠와 서비스를 즐김에 따라 젊은 세대 사 이에 더욱 인기가 있다.) 18) ⑤: 소비자 개인의 영화 및 비디오 시청 기록에 부합하는 비디오 추천과 같은 서비스가 소비자에게 큰 만족을 가져다준다고 언급하고 있으므로, ⑤ ‘비디오 추천 서 비스는 소비자의 시청 기록보다 무작위로 선택된 콘텐 츠를 우선시한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 과거에 사람들은 극장에 가거나 그들이 원하는 비 디오를 구매함으로써만 영화를 볼 수 있었다. ② 오늘날에는 스마트폰과 다른 디지털 기기들이 사람 들에게 온라인에서 엄청난 선택지의 영화에 대한 접근 을 제공한다. ③ 온라인 플랫폼은 기업들이 개별 고객에게 맞춘 매우 개인화된 제품과 서비스를 전달할 수 있도록 한다. ④ 기업들은 고객의 요구, 선호, 소비 패턴을 분석하여 만족도를 높이는 특화된 선택을 제공한다. 19) overconsumption, financial, unnecessary 제시문 구독 경제는 과소비와 재정적 부담을 초래할 수 있 으므로, 불필요한 구독을 정기적으로 평가하고 중단하는 것 이 중요하다. 20) ③: (A) 초기의 구독 경제의 예시로서, 우리에게 이미 익숙 한 우유와 신문 같은 제품들이 언급되므로, 구독 경제 의 개념이 새로운 것이 아니라는 흐름으로 not 뒤에 novel(새로운)이 알맞다. 본문변형 new → novel familiar 친숙한 (B) 일회성 히트 상품 대신이라고 했으며, 새 콘텐츠, 보다 개인 맞춤형, 업데이트 접근성 같은 예시가 언급 되므로, 기업들이 지속적 가치를 제공하는 것을 우선시 하여 고객들에게 많은 혜택을 준다는 흐름이 되는 lasting(오래 지속되는)이 알맞다. short-lived 오래가지 않는, 잠깐 동안의 본문변형 continuing → lasting (C) 글의 앞부분에서 구독 경제가 요즘 인기 있는 경제 모델이라고 했으며, 소비 추세의 변화들과 온라인 플랫 폼의 급성장이 두 개의 주요한 동인이라고 설명하므로, 구독 경제의 부상을 언급하는 흐름이 되는 rise(대두, 부상)가 알맞다. fall 몰락, 쇠퇴

W: Let’s talk about crowdfunding, a word combining
crowd and funding, meaning raising funds from
the public. When a project with insufficient funds
is shared online, people invest to reach a funding
goal within a set time frame. The most widely
used type of funding is reward-based. People give
money and, in return, get something like a product
or special experience. (A) Supporters have the
chance to be the first to receive and use it
before others, enjoying various benefits, such as
discounts and gifts. (B) People give money because
they believe in a cause or mission, not expecting
any rewards. (C) It’s used for projects that help
people in need and makes funds accessible to
all. (D) I believe crowdfunding makes it easier
for people to get money for their ideas because
people can support and buy things they believe
in. (E) Everyone is able to succeed and build a
better economy through crowdfunding.

위 담화를 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What does the term ‘crowdfunding’ refer to?
What happens when a project that lacks fundingis shared online?
How much of a discount do backers receive onaverage in reward-based crowdfunding?
How are the funds contributed in support of acause or mission utilized?
Why is it easier to secure funding for an ideathrough crowdfunding?

Jiyun, a high school student, starts her day by
logging in to a music streaming service on her
smartphone. She enjoys listening to her favorite
music, discovering new songs, and exploring new
artists every day. For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun
receives a delivery from a subscription service that
provides fresh vegetables and fruits. (A)방과 후에, 지
윤이는 그녀가 흥미를 느끼는 것마다 그녀의 지식을
확장하기 위해 비디오 강의 서비스를 활용한다. For
example, she watches various academic lectures to
review her schoolwork and stay updated about the
latest knowledge in her chosen field of study.
During weekends, Jiyun and her family spend
quality time together watching movies or dramas
using a streaming service.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how Jiyun manages her time while using variousdigital services
the different types of digital content Jiyun enjoysin her free time
the harmful effects of excessive reliance on digitalservices an teenagers

A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a
psychology
professor
at
Cornell
University,
reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t
spend your money on things. We assume that the
happiness we get from buying something will last
as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The
trouble with things is that ⓐ_________________________.
There are three critical reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. What once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
get used to a new possession, we look for an even
better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to
compare themselves with others. We buy a new car
and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better
one, and there’s always someone with a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we
are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves
than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can
really like your material stuff. You can even think that
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On
the other hand, your experiences really are part of
you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

The most popular block parties were those hosted
by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding
father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday
in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to extend the drum

of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.
Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential
in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and ⓒ[use / using] the break to show off their
individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the
people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls,
short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people
began to dance in groups in the streets and build
a street dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the
crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the beat”
and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning of
rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both DJing
and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked
a friend to take the role of addressing the audience,
that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their
parties. This separate role became MCing.

After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. Abandoned
buildings and parking lots ⓐ[used / were used] for
events
called
block
parties.
What
eventually
emerged from these parties? A vibrant youth
movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing,
breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang
violence with music, dance, art, and style.
The most popular block parties were those hosted
by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding
father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday
in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to extend the drum
section known as the break. No longer ⓑ[people
had / did people have] to stop dancing at the end
of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc.
Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential
in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and ⓒ[use / using] the break to show off their
individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the
people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls,
short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people
began to dance in groups in the streets and build
a street dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the
crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the beat”
and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning of
rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both DJing
and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked
a friend to take the role of addressing the audience,
that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their
parties. This separate role became MCing.

Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of
early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the
DJ or the rapper. However, a significant shift
occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the
1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of
life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy
who was born there and had to live and die as a
second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose
original aim was _______________________________________,
started a new tradition of social criticism against
injustice. The Message became one of the most
influential rap singles of all time, and was followed
by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same
time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping
made people move or dance. People heard the
social message while moving to the beat.

choices: encouraging competition through partying

urging rappers to concentrate on recent politicalissues
bringing about peace through shared music anddancing
resolving conflicts among generations by meansof parties

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final
sound of a word. Most often, (A)it is consciously
used for a musical effect in the final position of
lines within poems or songs. Let’s look at three
ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.
First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this
is called an end rhyme, which is the most
representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the
following example aloud.
My house is so big you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an
ending sound “op.”
Second, words can rhyme within the same line.
This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a
word in the middle of a line and another word in
the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn
Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For
example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not
exactly rhyme, but (B)they create a pattern of
similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect
rhymes, the consonants are identical while the
vowel sounds are different, or the other way round.
When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken
aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This
helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear,
and evokes emotions. So, if you create a rap,
rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger
and reach your listeners.

다음 글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

which] his days of freedom were over by moving

beat,
chanting,

The

at parties like “Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy
hop-bop,” “I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby,
hip-hip-hop and you don’t stop.” Such lines became
a standard part of rap and were included in the
lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s
Delight (1979), which ⓒ[was / were] an immediate
success.
ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: to bethatwas

solution: ⓐ ‘~라고 말해지다’라는 뜻의 ‘be said+to부정사’에서 주절의 시제보다 앞선 일인 경우 완료부정사(to+have+p.p.)를 사용해 야 하므로, to have been이 알맞다. ⓑ 동사 reminded와 간접목적어인 him, 삽입된 부사구 in a jokey way 뒤에 이어진 직접목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(his days of freedom were over)을 이끌어 ’remind+간접목적어+ 직접목적어(that절)(~에게 …하다는 것을 상기시키다)‘의 4형식 구문을 이루어야 하므로, 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다. ⓒ 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이므로 선 행사에 수를 일치시켜야 하며, 관계사절이 부연 설명하는 선행 사 Rapper’s Delight (1979)가 단수이므로, 단수형 과거동사 was가 알맞다. W: Good morning, students! Today, we’re going to
learn about “pop culture.” (A)____________, popular
culture, also called mass culture or pop culture,
refers to ideas, practices, and trends that are
popular and widespread in everyday life. Second,
it includes movies, music, fashion, and dance.
Even
online
contents
such
as
webtoons,
streaming series, and social media challenges
have become popular genres in pop culture.
Third, pop culture significantly influences our
society. Whether it’s driving changes in fashion or
starting a social movement, pop culture, which
spreads through mass media and online platforms,
leaves a lasting impact. A good example is the
“Ice Bucket Challenge,” which evolved into a
global fundraising event. (B)____________, pop culture
isn’t just about what’s “cool.” It’s a mirror of
society, reflecting and shaping who we are.

위 담화의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
choices: HoweverIn fact
First of allIn short
For instanceLikewise
First of allSimilarly
For exampleTo sum up
solution: (A) 오늘 배우게 될 주제로 ‘대중문화’를 소개한 뒤, 주제와 관 련된 첫 번째 주요 내용으로서 대중문화의 정의를 말하고, 이 어서 Second(둘째)와 Third(셋째)를 사용해 대중문화에 포함되 는 요소, 대중문화의 영향을 차례대로 설명하고 있으므로, ‘우 선, 가장 먼저’를 뜻하는 First of all이 알맞다. (B) 대중문화의 사회적 영향력에 대해 설명하고 그 예시로 ‘아 이스 버킷 챌린지’를 언급한 뒤, 대중문화가 단지 ‘멋진 것’에 관한 것이 아니라 우리의 모습을 반영하고 형성하는 사회의 거울이라고 말하며 전체 글의 내용을 정리 요약하고 있으므로, In short(요컨대) 또는 To sum up(요약하자면)이 알맞다.

body:
Imagine an urban area ⓐthat is fast becoming a
slum after an economic recession. Businesses close
their doors and building owners have left. The area
is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating
even in winter. Only those who can’t afford to move
out remain. Unemployment is high, many gangs
emerge, and gang violence between young people
ⓑbecome an everyday thing. Despair is on every
street corner. One day, however, a gang called the
Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its
free meal and medical care programs, decides to
stop fighting and instead persuade young people
ⓒto unite and create a better community. They
suggest a peace treaty. “This is for peace, men. The
violence took away our brothers. We’re not gangsters
anymore. We’ve got to make this town a better
place to live.” Thanks to these new voices, gang
leaders from all over the area sign the treaty. Never
again will they use violence to solve their disputes.
This is the Bronx in the New York of the early
1970s, ⓓwhich hip-hop music was born as a major
part of a new culture of peace created by African
Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop,
now one of the world’s most dominant music
genres, is a ⓔfascinating one. Let’s explore it.

윗글의 첫 번째 문단의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the power of hip-hop in overcoming violenceand despair
the increasing need for community medical careand free meals
the social effects of immigration on Americanurban development
government programs for reducing crime inpoor urban neighborhoods
the desperate situation of a city and a gang’sproposal of a peace treaty to address it
solution: 경기 침체 후 빠르게 슬럼가로 변해가며 젊은이들 사이에 갱 단 폭력이 일상이 된 어느 도시 지역에서 한 갱단이 싸움을 멈추고 젊은이들이 단결해 더 나은 공동체를 만들자고 설득하 기로 결정하여 평화 협정을 제안하고, 이에 지역 전역의 갱단 대표들이 모여 협정에 서명한다는 내용이므로, 글의 주제로 ❺ ‘한 도시의 암울한 상황과 그것을 해결하기 위한 한 갱단의 평 화 협정 제안’이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

body:
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. Abandoned
buildings and parking lots were used for events
called block parties. What eventually emerged from
these parties? A ⓐvibrant youth movement called
hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing,
MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with
music, dance, art, and style.
(A)가장 인기 있는 블록 파티들은 디제이 Kool Herc
에 의해 주최된 것들이었고, 그는 힙합의 창시자로 간
주된다. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday in
August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to ⓑreduce the drum
section known as the break. No longer did people
have to stop dancing at the end of the record
while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool Herc’s style
of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of
hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and use the break to show off their individual
dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing
to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, ⓒshort for
Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to
dance in groups in the streets and build a street
dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over ⓓinstrumental parts of songs to excite
the crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the
beat” and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning
of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both
DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they
asked a friend to take the role of (B)________________
________________________, that is, of the Master of
Ceremonies or MC, at their parties. This ⓔseparate
role became MCing.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: changing records
teaching how to rap
organizing block parties
addressing the audience
coordinating dancers’ movements
solution: Kool Herc와 같은 디제이들이 관중의 흥을 돋우기 위해 박자 와 라임을 넣은 말을 했다는 설명 뒤에 그들이 디제잉과 리듬 감 있는 외침을 동시에 할 수가 없었을 때의 상황이 제시되었 고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 that is(즉)로 사회자 곧 엠씨가 언급되므로, 친구에게 자신을 대신해 관중에게 말을 하는 진행자의 역할을 부탁했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘청중에 게 말하는 것’이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

Then where did the word hip-hop originate from?
Nobody knows the exact origin, but (A)it is said
that the word hip-hop was first used at a block
party. A young man at the party was about (B)to
join the army. His good friend, the MC of the
party, reminded him in a jokey way (C)that his days
of freedom were over by moving across the stage
like a military instructor to the beat, chanting,
“Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop.” The crowd loved it.
After that, MCs (D)tried out new lines at parties like
“Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy hop-bop,” “I said a
hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby, hip-hip-hop and you
don’t stop.” Such lines became a standard part of
rap and were included in the lyrics of the first
recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s Delight (1979),
which was an immediate success.
The new music and dancing spread very fast.
There was a sharp unexplained decline in violence
during the 1980s in New York. One police officer
asked a boy on the street (E)if he knew why. The
boy said, “It’s because they’re dancing.”

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

(A) The Message became one of the most influential
rap singles of all time, and was followed by
many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the
same time, their music with its rhythmic beat
and rapping made people move or dance.
People heard the social message while moving
to the beat.
(B) This song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh
realities of life in the ghetto, including the sad
story of a boy who was born there and had to
live and die as a second-class citizen. With this

of social criticism against injustice.
(C) However, a significant shift occurred during the

importantly, the appearance of The Message by
the group Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five
in 1982 was groundbreaking.
solution: 랩 가사는 일반적으로 다 함께 즐거운 시간을 갖자는 내용과 디제이나 래퍼의 능력을 뽐내는 내용에 초점을 두었다는 내용 의 주어진 글 다음에, However(그러나)로 시작하여 1980년대 힙합 음악의 부상 시기에 랩 가사에 중요한 변화가 일어났다 는 반전의 상황을 제시한 후, 무엇보다 <The Message(메시 지)>라는 노래의 등장이 획기적이었다는 점을 언급한 (C), <The Message(메시지)>를 This song(이 노래)으로 가리켜 이 노래의 가사는 게토에서의 삶의 가혹한 현실을 자세히 묘사했 으며 이 노래를 통해 힙합이 불의에 저항하는 새로운 사회 비 판의 전통을 시작했다는 (B), <The Message(메시지)>는 역사 상 가장 영향력 있는 랩 싱글 중 하나가 되었고, 1980년대와 1990년대에 인종 차별에 맞서는 많은 힙합 노래가 그 뒤를 이 었다는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. Hip-hop music began to be a way to express
respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop
pioneers. (A) For rappers, the pioneers are heroes
who overcame hardship and injustice and ⓐ[go /

Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot
have ⓑ[so / too] much respect for these heroes. (C)
The phrase “something from nothing,” often used to

ⓑ
ⓒ

solution: ⓐ 흐름상 주절의 동사 are가 아니라 주격 관계대명사 who가 이끄는 절의 첫 번째 동사 overcame과 등위접속사 and에 의 해 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, 과거동사 went가 알맞다. ⓑ ’아무리 ~해도 지나치지 않다‘라는 뜻의 ’cannot+동사원형 +too+형용사+명사‘ 구조를 이루어야 하므로, too가 알맞다. ⓒ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(developed ~ resources) 을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 early hip-hoppers를 부연 설명하 는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 사람 선행사와 쓰이는 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 who가 알맞다.

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final
sound of a word. Most often, it is (A)[consciously /
unintentionally] used for a musical effect in the final
position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look
at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.
First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this
is called an end rhyme, which is the most
representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the
following example aloud.
My house is so big you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an
ending sound “op.”
Second, words can rhyme within the same line.
This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a
word in the middle of a line and another word in
the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn
Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For
example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not
exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of
(B)[similar / dissimilar] sounds /s/ and /t/. In most
imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while
the vowel sounds are different, or ⓐthe other way
round.
When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken
aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This
helps the song keep a steady beat, (C)[offends /
pleases] the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you
create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your
voice stronger and reach your listeners.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: consciously      dissimilar    pleases
unintentionally      similar    pleases
consciously      similar    offends
unintentionally      dissimilar    offends
consciously      similar    pleases
solution: (A) 라임은 시나 노래에서 음악적 효과를 주기 위해 사용된다 는 내용이 이어지므로, 라임이 의도적으로 사용된다는 흐름이 되는 consciously(의식적으로)가 알맞다. (B) ‘start’, ‘sport’, ‘straight’는 비슷한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만드는 단어들의 예시이므로, 이 세 단어들이 정확히 라임을 이루진 않지만 유사한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만든다는 흐름이 되는 similar(유사한)가 알맞다. (C) 라임을 이루는 일련의 단어들을 큰 소리로 말하면 리듬감 있는 패턴 또는 ‘흐름’이 만들어지며, 이는 노래가 안정된 박자를 유지하도록 돕는다는 내용에 이어지므로, 듣는 이의 귀를 즐겁 게 한다는 흐름이 되는 pleases(~을 기쁘게 하다)가 알맞다.

body:
Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of
early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the
DJ or the rapper. ⓐ______________, a significant shift
occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the
1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of
life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy
who was born there and had to live and die as a
second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose
original aim was creating peace through partying,
started a new tradition of social criticism against
injustice. The Message became one of the most
influential rap singles of all time, and was followed
by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same
time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping
made people move or dance. People heard the
social message while moving to the beat.
Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop
lyrics, which can be summarized as “respect.”
Hip-hop music began to be a way to express
respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop
pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who
overcame hardship and injustice and went on to
create new music and culture. ⓑ_____________, many
hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much
respect for these heroes. The phrase “something
from nothing,” often used to summarize the genre’s
history, is also an expression of admiration for early
hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the
ghetto despite very limited resources. Rappers also
proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and
perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in
a similar way to the pioneers. This is why the
message of respect is about both self-worth and
respect for others. ⓒ힙합에서 존경이라는 개념의 중
요성은 아무리 강하게 강조해도 지나치지 않다.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ                    ⓑ
choices: HoweverFurthermore
HoweverHence
SimilarlyMeanwhile
ConsequentlyBesides
As a resultTherefore
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a
slum after an economic recession. Businesses close
their doors and building owners have left. The area
is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating
even in winter. Only those who can’t afford to
move out remain.
(A) They suggest a peace treaty. “This is for peace,
men. The violence took away our brothers.
We’re not gangsters anymore. We’ve got to
make this town a better place to live.”
(B) One day, however, a gang called the Ghetto
Brothers, which is respected because of its free
meal and medical care programs, decides to
stop fighting and instead persuade young
people to unite and create a better community.
(C) Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and
gang violence between young people becomes an
everyday thing. Despair is on every street corner.
Thanks to these new voices, gang leaders from all
over the area sign the treaty. ⓐ그들은 결코 다시는 그
들의 분쟁을 해결하기 위해 폭력을 사용하지 않을 것이다.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 경기 침체 후 빠르게 슬럼가로 변해가는 한 도시 지역의 상황 을 가정하며 기업들이 문을 닫고 주인들이 떠나버리면서 버려 진 건물들이 가득하고, 겨울에도 난방이 되지 않고 이사 갈 여 력이 없는 사람들만 남아 있는 문제를 언급하는 주어진 글 다 음에, 높은 실업률과 갱단 폭력의 일상화라는 다른 문제를 추 가 언급하며 곳곳에 절망이 퍼져 있다는 암울한 사회적 분위 기를 말하는 (C), however(그러나)를 사용해 Ghetto Brothers라 는 한 갱단이 싸움을 멈추고 단결하여 더 나은 공동체를 만들 자고 설득하기로 결정한다는 내용으로 상황을 전환하는 (B), Ghetto Brothers라는 갱단을 They로 가리켜 그들이 평화 협정 을 제안하며 이제 마을을 더 살기 좋은 곳으로 만들자고 목소 리를 낸다는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

body:
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. ⓐAbandoning
buildings and parking lots were used for events
called block parties. What eventually emerged from
these parties? A vibrant youth movement called
hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing,
MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with
music, dance, art, and style.
The most popular block parties were those hosted
by DJ Kool Herc, ⓑthat is regarded as the founding
father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s
birthday in August 1973 is now known as the
birthplace of hip-hop music because of his new DJ
technique. At this party, ⓒusing two turntables at
the same time, Herc played two copies of the same
record and then switched between them to extend
the drum section known as the break. No longer
did people have to stop dancing at the end of the
record while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool
Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential in
the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and use the break to show off their individual
dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing
to
his
music
B-Boys
and
B-Girls,
short
for
Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to
dance in groups in the streets and ⓓbuild a street
dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite
the crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the
beat” and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning
of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both
DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they
asked a friend ⓔtaking the role of addressing the
audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or
MC, at their parties. This separate role became
MCing.

the characteristics of Kool Herc’s style of DJingin early hip-hop
the influence of breakdancing on the evolutionof hip-hop culture
the gradual decline in the popularity of MCingwithin the B-Boy and B-Girl community
the birth of hip-hop culture and its developmentinfluenced by Kool Herc’s innovative DJ techniques

A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final
sound of a word. Most often, it is consciously used
for a musical effect in the final position of lines
within poems or songs. Let’s look at three ways
ⓐthat rhyme is used in rap lyrics.
First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this
is called an end rhyme, which is the most
representative kind of rhyme. ⓑTry reading the
following example aloud.
My house is so big ⓒthat you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an
ending sound “op.”
Second, words can rhyme within the same line.
This creates an internal rhyme, which ⓓinvolve a
word in the middle of a line and another word in
the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn
Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For
example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not
exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar
sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the
consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are
different, or the other way round.
When a sequence of rhymed words ⓔis spoken
aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This
helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear,
and ⓕevoke emotions. So, if you create a rap,
rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger
and reach your listeners.

choices: Why Rhyming Matters in Rap Lyrics
Perfect Rhymes: The Key to Successful Rap
How Rappers Come Up with Great Rhymes
The Types and Effects of Rhymes in Rap Lyrics
The Emotional Power of Rhyming in Rap Lyrics

early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and (A)boasting about the ability of
the DJ or the rapper. However, a (B)significant shift
occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the
1980s. Most importantly, the (C)appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics (D)detailed the harsh realities
of life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a

became one of the most influential rap singles of
all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs

Our final destination was Uluru, the largest rock in
the world. I’ve longed to see it in person ever since
I came across a picture of it a few years ago.
When I finally laid eyes on Uluru after an
exhausting train ride, I couldn’t believe ⓐthat I was
seeing. Could this gigantic mountain really be a
single piece of rock? From a distance, it looked like
a huge red dome, ⓑwas providing an amazing
contrast against the clear blue sky.
 The next day, we walked around its 10-kilometer
base. Along the way, we saw numerous caves,
ⓒsome of them displayed a distinct gray hue. My
uncle informed me that Uluru was naturally gray,
but that its iron content had oxidized over time,
giving it its iconic red color.
 The highlight of our visit was the sunset. Prior to
my trip, I had learned that the color of the sunsets
at Uluru ⓓchange over time based on the sun’s
position and the intensity of sunlight. When I finally
saw one, the colors transformed from red to deep
orange and then to purple as the sun sank below
the horizon. It was impossible ⓔto be found words
to describe the beauty I was seeing. It was the
most memorable night of my entire journey.

Kakadu National Park is the largest national park
in northern Australia. Although the trip was long
and tiring, the park’s natural beauty immediately
revitalized us. The landscape resembled an ocean
filled with green eucalyptus trees, and the air was
incredibly refreshing! Perhaps the only drawback
was that being in a remote region, we had no
Wi-Fi connection. (A)_____________, we quickly adapted
and embraced the quiet and peaceful vacation
atmosphere.
 One of the highlights of our visit there was our
tour led by Victor, an Aboriginal guide. He
explained that Kakadu has been home to Aboriginal
people for over 40,000 years. He also introduced us
to rock art sites depicting Aboriginal stories. ⓐ내가
특히 흥미롭게 느낀 한 그림은 엑스레이 스타일로 그
려진 것으로, 어떤 부분들을 먹을 수 있는지 보여 주
기 위해 물고기의 내부를 묘사한 것이었다. Other
fascinating drawings showed things like a spirit
creating lightning and a hunter holding a spear.
 (B)_____________, Kakadu is famous for its saltwater
crocodiles, as there are around 10,000 living in the
region. They are the largest of all crocodile species
and grow up to six meters long! While crossing the
Yellow River, we spotted over 30 of them! Being
able to see them right in front of me was an
experience that I will never forget.

(A)
(B)
choices: HoweverIn fact
As a resultTherefore
For exampleConversely
For instanceIn addition
NeverthelessFurthermore
solution: (A) Kakadu 국립 공원은 외딴 지역이라 Wi-Fi가 없었다는 단점 을 언급한 후, 우리는 그것에 빠르게 적응하고 평화로운 분위 기를 받아들였다는 긍정의 흐름이 이어지므로, However(하지 만) 또는 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)가 알맞다. (B) Kakadu 국립 공원에서 원주민 이야기를 묘사한 암각화 유적 지를 가이드에게서 소개받았다는 설명에 이어, Kakadu의 볼거리 로 약 10,000마리의 바다악어로도 유명하다는 설명이 이어지므 로, ‘게다가’라는 뜻의 In addition 또는 Furthermore가 알맞다.

seeing. Could this ⓑmodest mountain really be a
single piece of rock? From a distance, it looked like
a huge red dome, providing an amazing ⓒcontrast
against the clear blue sky.
 The next day, we walked around its 10-kilometer
base. Along the way, we saw numerous caves, some
of which displayed a distinct gray hue. My uncle
informed me that Uluru was naturally gray, but that
its iron content had ⓓoxidized over time, giving it
its iconic red color.
 The highlight of our visit was the sunset. Prior to

at Uluru changes over time based on the sun’s

orange and then to purple as the sun sank below

the horizon. It was impossible to find words to
describe the beauty I was seeing. It was the most
(C)[memorable / forgettable] night of my entire
journey.

(C)

solution: (A) 몇 년 전에 Uluru의 사진을 우연히 접한 이후로 그것을 직 접 보기를 열망해 왔다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ‘직접’이라는 뜻의 firsthand가 적절하다. (B) 수많은 동굴들을 보았는데 그것들 중 일부는 뚜렷한 회색 이었다는 내용에 이어지고 있으며, 삼촌의 설명에 따르면 시간 이 지나며 철 성분이 산화되어 붉은색이 되었다고 했으므로 원래는 회색이었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘원래, 자연 적으로’라는 뜻의 naturally가 적절하다. (C) Uluru의 일몰 모습을 보며 감탄하며 자신이 보고 있는 아 름다움을 묘사할 단어를 찾는 것이 불가능했다는 내용에 이어 지고 있으므로 여행 전체에서 가장 기억에 남은 밤이었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘기억에 남는’이라는 뜻의 memorable이 적절하다. 동아(박용예) 2과

One of the highlights of our visit there was our
tour led by Victor, an Aboriginal guide. He
explained that Kakadu has been home to Aboriginal
people for over 40,000 years. He also introduced us
to rock art sites depicting Aboriginal stories. One
drawing that I found particularly interesting was
done in an X-ray style, illustrating the insides of a
fish to show which parts were edible. Other
fascinating drawings showed things like a spirit
creating lightning and a hunter holding a spear.
Kakadu is also famous for its saltwater crocodiles,
as there are around 10,000 living in the region.
They are the largest of all crocodile species and
grow up to six meters long! While crossing the
Yellow River, we spotted over 30 of them! Being
able to see them right in front of me was an
experience that I will never forget.

상쾌했다.③ 가이드 Victor는 우리에게 암각화 유적지를 소개했고, 나는 X선 스타일의 물고기 그림이 특히 흥미롭다고생각했다.④ Kakadu는 바다악어로 유명하며, 그 지역에는 약10,000마리가 살고 있다.12) ②: ⓑ modest((규모 등이) 별로 크지 않은) → gigantic(거대한)13) ④: 글쓴이가 세계에서 가장 큰 바위인 Uluru를 지역을 탐험하는 것의 어려움⑤ Uluru를 둘러싼 자연환경과 계절에 따른 그것의 변화14) ③: 우리는 Uluru의 10킬로미터에 달하는 바닥 주변을 걷는도중 수많은 동굴들을 보았는데, 그중 일부는 뚜렷한회색이었다고 언급하고 있으므로, ③ ‘Uluru의 10킬로미터에 달하는 바닥 주변을 걸으면서, 우리는 수많은 동굴을 보았고, 그들 모두는 눈에 띄는 붉은빛을 띠고 있었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.오답① 몇 년 전에, 글쓴이는 Uluru의 사진을 우연히 접했고, 그것을 직접 보기를 원해왔다.② 글쓴이는 Uluru를 처음 보았을 때 깜짝 놀랐는데,그것은 멀리서 보기에 거대한 붉은색을 띤 돔처럼 보였기 때문이다.④ 우리의 Uluru 방문에서 하이라이트였던 것은 바로일몰이었다.⑤ 글쓴이는 해 질 무렵 Uluru의 모습이 말로 표현하기어려울 정도로 아름답다고 느꼈다.15) ②: 어법상 알맞은 것은 총 3개이다.ⓑ invited와 목적어 me에 이어져 ‘invite+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하도록 초대하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는목적격보어 자리로, invite는 목적격보어로 to부정사를취하는 동사이므로 to join은 적절하다.ⓕ 주어 My trip to Australia(나의 호주 여행)이 fill(~을채우다)의 대상이므로 ‘fill A with B(A를 B로 채우다)’의수동 표현인 ‘A be filled with B’를 써야 한다. 따라서was filled with는 적절하다.ⓖ four of와 정관사 the, 최상급 형태의 형용사 mostmemorable에 이어져 있으므로 ‘가장 ~한 …들 중 네개’라는 뜻의 ‘four of+the+최상급+복수명사(구)’를 이루는 복수명사 destinations는 적절하다.오답ⓐ spend → to spend (앞의 명사구 the remarkableopportunity를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 자리이므로 spend는 to spend로 고친다.)ⓒ Known → Knowing (완전한 절이 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되어 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절의 주어 he가 ‘알고 있는’ 주체이므로Known은 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 Knowing으로 고친다.)ⓓ had been left → had left (앞의 명사구 the humidheat를 선행사로 하는 목적격 관계대명사절의 동사 자리로 주절의 주어인 I가 멜버른에 도착하여 쌀쌀한 공기를 맞이했던(was) 것보다 한국에 습한 무더위를 두고왔던 것이 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거 완료(hadp.p.)를 사용한 것은 알맞으나, 주어인 I가 ‘두고 왔던’주체이므로 과거완료 능동태로 써야 한다. 따라서 hadbeen left는 had left로 고친다. 참고로 the humid heat와 I 사이에 목적격 관계대명사 that 또는 which가 생략되었다.)ⓔ Realize → Realizing 또는 To realize (동사 made에대한 주어가 필요하므로, 이어지는 간접의문문 where Iwas를 목적어로 취하여 주어부를 이루는 동명사(구) 또는 to부정사(구)가 되어야 한다. 따라서 Realize를Realizing 또는 To Realize로 고친다.)*ⓔ는 원래 지문에서 Realizing이었음16) ⑤: (A) 과거형 동사 found의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(Ifound particularly interesting)을 이끌어 선행사 Onedrawing을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.(B) 앞의 명사구 a spirit를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는분사 자리이며 수식을 받는 a spirit이 ‘만드는’ 주체이며 목적어인 명사 lightning이 이어지고 있으므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 creating이 적절하다.(C) 주어가 동명사구인 Being ~ me이며 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급하므로 be동사 단수형인 was가 적절하다.17) ⑤: 글쓴이는 Kakadu에서 원주민 가이드 Victor가 이끄는 투어를 통해 4만 년 넘게 이어진 원주민 문화와 암각화를살펴보고, 옐로우 리버(Yellow River)에서 바다악어를 직접 관찰한 잊지 못할 경험을 했다는 내용의 글이므로,글의 요지로 ⑤ ‘글쓴이는 Kakadu 국립공원에서 원주민문화를 경험하고 야생동물을 마주했다.’가 알맞다.오답① 글쓴이는 Kakadu의 원주민들과 그들의 전통적인 생활 방식에 대해 알게 되었다.② 글쓴이는 Kakadu의 원주민들과 야생동물 사이의 관계를 탐구했다.③ 글쓴이는 Kakadu의 문화유산과 자연유산이 어떻게보존되어 왔는지를 알게 되었다.④ 글쓴이는 다양한 야생동물을 통해 Kakadu의 생태학적 중요성을 발견했다.18) ④: (A) 몇 년 전에 Uluru의 사진을 우연히 접한 이후로 그것을 직접 보기를 열망해 왔다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로‘직접’이라는 뜻의 firsthand가 적절하다.virtually 가상으로본문변형 in person → firsthand(B) 수많은 동굴들을 보았는데 그것들 중 일부는 뚜렷한 회색이었다는 내용에 이어지고 있으며, 삼촌의 설명에 따르면 시간이 지나며 철 성분이 산화되어 붉은색이되었다고 했으므로 원래는 회색이었다는 흐름이 되어야한다. 따라서 ‘원래, 자연적으로’라는 뜻의 naturally가적절하다.artificially 인위적으로(C) Uluru의 일몰 모습을 보며 감탄하며 자신이 보고있는 아름다움을 묘사할 단어를 찾는 것이 불가능했다는 내용에 이어지고 있으므로 여행 전체에서 가장 기억에 남은 밤이었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘기억에 남는’이라는 뜻의 memorable이 적절하다.forgettable 금방 잊혀지는, 기억에 남지 않는19) ③: 글쓴이는 동물과 자연에 대한 열정을 바탕으로 삼촌과함께 호주에서 한 달간 생태 관광을 하며 놀라운 장소와 자연을 경험했다고 설명하고 있으므로, 멜버른 사람들과 한국 사람들 사이의 생활방식 차이를 언급한 (C)‘눈에 띄는 한 가지 차이점은 멜버른 사람들이 한국 사람들보다 일상생활에서 더 여유로운 생활 속도를 중시하는 경향이 있다는 것이다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.20) ⑤: Kakadu 국립 공원의 유일한 단점이 외딴 지역에 있어서 와이파이 연결이 없다는 내용에 역접의 연결사However로 연결되어 있으며 Kakadu 국립 공원에서 원주민 가이드에게 그 지역의 역사와 암각화에 대한 설명을 들으며 바다악어를 보는 등의 경험을 하는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘빠르게적응하고 조용하고 평화로운 휴가 분위기를 받아들였다’가 알맞다.오답① 여전히 자연 풍경을 즐기기는 했지만, 인터넷을 사용할 수 없는 것을 아쉬워했다② 안정적인 인터넷 접속이 되지 않는 것에 점차 불만을 느끼게 되었다③ 평화로운 주변 환경이 우리가 기대했던 것만큼 즐겁지는 않다고 느꼈다④ 결국 평화로운 주변 환경을 즐기기보다는 계속 바쁘게 지내는 것을 선택했다

you
wish
you
could
experience
an
unforgettable part of nature? The Salar de Uyuni

America, Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in
the
world
and
offers
a
truly
exceptional

body:
다음 주어진 대화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

M: Narae, how about taking a family trip this
holiday?
G: Sounds fun, Dad! Do you have any specific place
in mind?
(A) We can take great pictures of traditional houses
and enjoy cultural activities like making Korean
fans and hanji.
(B) Let’s visit both places. They are close to each
other. We can spend the first two days in
Gunsan and the last two in Jeonju.
(C) I was thinking of Gunsan. There are many historical
sites and museums, along with fun activities
such as ziplining, boating, and fishing.
(D) Oh, I went there years ago, and the food was
amazing.
(E) That sounds interesting, but I prefer to visit
places with good food and great photo spots.
How about Jeonju?
G: That’s a terrific idea!
solution: 가족 여행을 제안하는 아빠의 말에 나래가 특정 장소를 생각 하고 있는지 묻고 있으므로 군산을 고려하고 있다고 하면서 군산에서 할 수 있는 활동들을 소개하는 (C)가 가장 먼저 오 고, 다음으로 그것은 흥미롭게 들리지만 자신은 맛있는 음식과 사진 촬영을 선호한다고 하면서 전주를 제안하는 (E), 전주를 there로 가리키며 그곳에 가 본 적이 있으며 음식이 맛있었다 는 (D), 전주에서 할 수 있는 다양한 활동들을 소개하는 (A), 이에 아빠가 동의하며 군산과 전주 두 곳 모두 방문하자고 제 안하는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 동아(박용예) 2과

Our first destination was Phillip Island, ⓐwhich is
just a two-hour drive from Melbourne and is
famous for its “penguin parade.” This unique parade
features little blue penguins, measuring only 35 to
42 centimeters in height ─slightly bigger than a
bowling pin! When we arrived at the beach, we
were
guided
to
carefully
ⓑdesigned
viewing
platforms to avoid disturbing the penguins. We
were also ⓒprohibiting from taking photos, as
bright lights and sudden flashes could frighten
them.
 The penguin parade took place in the evening
ⓓwhen the penguins returned from the ocean to
the shore. The penguins leave their burrows early in
the morning, spend the day fishing, and then come
home to feed their young and rest. Everyone
watched silently as these little two-legged creatures
returned
home.
Hundreds
of
penguins,
each
incredibly cute, created an unforgettable sight! We
even saw some baby penguins ⓔto come to greet
their parents, which was a heartwarming sight.
 After the parade, we explored the visitor center,
ⓕwhich we saw colorful penguin jumpers placed
over toy penguins. These jumpers (A)_________________
______________ during the big oil spill of 2001. They
kept the penguins from swallowing the oil that
stuck to their feathers. It was touching to learn how
many people cared about the penguins and tried
their best ⓖto protect them in creative ways.

played a significant role

body:
One of the sites I was most excited about was the
Great Barrier Reef, the world’s largest coral reef
system. There are several regions you can visit to
see it, and I chose to explore Lady Elliot Island in
the southern region, which is known for its
beautiful coral reefs and manta rays.
As our plane approached land, I spotted the Great
Barrier Reef, ⓐstretching as far as I could see. The
water was different shades of blue and green,
depending on the depth of the sea and the coral
formations underneath. Endless patches of white
sand added to the breathtaking scenery. It was so
beautiful, and I couldn’t wait to dive into the
crystal-clear water!
 As I wanted to explore the coral reef more closely,
I went snorkeling. The first sight that greeted me in
the water ⓑwas manta rays. Even though they are
endangered, I witnessed many mantas ⓒgliding
elegantly through the water. I also encountered sea
turtles and a school of tropical fish. It was the coral
reef, however, ⓓthat impressed me the most that
day. It was a spectacular burst of colors and life!
My uncle later informed me ⓔthat many parts of
the Great Barrier Reef, especially in the northern
region, suffer from coral bleaching, which turns the
reef white. I felt bad when I heard that and hoped
the reef would recover soon.

윗글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

At Lady Elliot Island in the southern Great Barrier
Reef, the writer was impressed by the (A)___________
coral reefs and diverse marine life, but became
concerned about the (B)___________ caused by coral
bleaching in many parts of the reef.
(A)
(B)
choices: monotonousharm
artificialrecovery
colorfulgrowth
lifelesschange
vibrantdamage
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Our final destination was Uluru, the largest rock in
the world. I ⓐlonged to see it in person ever since
I came across a picture of it a few years ago.
When I finally laid eyes on Uluru after an exhausting
train ride, I couldn’t believe ⓑwhat I was seeing.
Could this gigantic mountain really be a single
piece of rock? From a distance, it looked like a
huge red dome, ⓒproviding an amazing contrast
against the clear blue sky.
 The next day, we walked around its 10-kilometer
base. Along the way, we saw numerous caves,
ⓓsome of them displayed a distinct gray hue. My
uncle informed me that Uluru was naturally gray,
but that its iron content had oxidized over time,
ⓔgiven it its iconic red color.
 The highlight of our visit was the sunset. (A)여행에

Hello, everyone. Today we’ll discuss how to
effectively set goals using SMART strategies. SMART
stands for “specific, measurable, achievable, relevant,
and
time-bound.”
When
setting
a
goal,
it’s
important to be specific about what you want to
achieve. And make your goal measurable so you
can check your progress. Your goal should also be
realistically possible to achieve and relevant to your
life. Lastly, set a time limit to achieve it. For

body:
[What to Change]
Give Yourself a New Identity
ⓐ당신은 며칠 이상 좋은 습관을 기르고 유지하는 것
이 어렵다고 생각할 수도 있다. This often happens
when people focus on changing external outcomes
or behaviors rather than on where they originate
from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you achieve. The
middle layer is process — what you do. The deepest
and most fundamental layer is identity — what you
believe or who you are. While changes in all three
layers are useful in their own way, the key to lasting
success lies in the direction of change. True
behavior change occurs when there is a shift in your
identity from within. If your new habit is not in
harmony with your identity, it is unlikely to last.
You can work on changing your identity through
two steps. First, keep asking yourself, “What kind of
person do I want to become?” Once you have an
idea of the kind of person you want to be, start
reinforcing
that
identity
through
your
actions.
Specifically, repeat the action that kind of person
would choose to do, and over time, you will
naturally become such a person. For example, if you
want to start exercising daily, think of yourself as
an energetic and motivated person who cares about
his or her health. Then try to do the routines that
such a person would naturally do. Repeating these
routines will gradually lead you to become that
kind of person.

When ⓐcreating a new habit, set a cue that
sparks the habit and ⓑmakes the cue as obvious
as possible. (A) The two most common cues are
time and location. (B) The formula for your action
plan can be “I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in
[LOCATION].” Instead of a vague intent like “I will
work out,” be specific and tell ⓒyou “I will work
out for an hour starting at 8 p.m. at home.”
(C) Your current habit is already associated with a
particular time and location, so ⓓpairing it with a new
one by saying something like “After I [CURRENT
HABIT], I will [NEW HABIT].” (D) Your action plan can
be “After I finish dinner around 8 p.m., I’ll immediately
change into my workout clothes.” (E) The more this
link between the cue and the action is repeated, ⓔthe
more firmly the new habit will be rooted in your life.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ makes → make (등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 명령문 동사 set과 병렬을 이루므로 동사원형 make로 고친다. that sparks the habit은 선행사 a cue를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사절이다. makes를 쓰면 관계사절의 동사 sparks와 병렬을 이루어 a cue 가 makes의 주어가 된다. 이때 목적어 the cue가 문맥상 주어 a cue와 동일한 대상을 가리키므로 재귀대명사 itself를 써야 하며, ‘단서가 자기 자신을 분명하게 만든다’라는 의미가 되어 본문의 의도와도 어긋난다.) ⓒ you → yourself (명령문의 생략된 주어는 you이며, tell의 목적어 가 주어와 같은 대상을 가리키므로 재귀대명사 yourself로 고친다.) ⓓ pairing → pair (등위접속사 so 뒤에서 새로운 습관과 현재 습관을 연결하라고 권하는 명령문이 이어져야 하므로, 동명사 pairing을 동사원형 pair로 고친다.)

body:
W: We often hear that self-care is important, but
what is it exactly and how can we do it?
[What is self-care?]
Lisa: I think self-care is loving yourself and making
sure that you’re okay physically and mentally.
Jake: I see self-care as a battery recharge.
Nari: Self-care is looking after yourself and checking
whether you can continue doing your daily
routine.
[Why is self-care important?]
Lisa: Self-care is important because it prevents
burnout and helps you manage your stress.
Jake: Through self-care, you can restore your energy
so that you can fully enjoy your life.
Nari: Self-care helps you improve and make better
decisions.
[What can you do in terms of self-care?]
Lisa: There are many different things you can do,
so it’s important to figure out what works for
you. As for me, I treat myself to delicious
food.
Jake: Being social is a big thing for me. When I
hang out with my family or friends, I feel
re-energized.
Nari: I like to watch cat videos. It gives me a sense
of healing. I strongly recommend it.

위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: For Lisa, self-care means loving herself andlooking after her body and mind.
Jake compares the effects of self-care tocharging up a drained battery.
Nari defines self-care as checking whether shecan keep up her daily routine.
Nari believes that watching cat videos helps hermake wiser everyday decisions.
Lisa treats herself to good food as a way oftaking care of herself.

A habit is an atomic routine that is easy to do

small improvements on a daily basis. Over time,
these
tiny

can
make
a
huge
difference in our lives. If you are seeking to build

Give Yourself a New Identity
You might find it (A)[easy / challenging] to develop
and ⓑmaintaining good habits for more than a few
days. This often happens when people focus on
ⓒchange external outcomes or behaviors rather than
on where they originate from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — ⓓwhat you achieve.
The middle layer is process — what you do. The
deepest and most (B)[fundamental / superficial]
layer is identity — what you believe or who you are.
While changes in all three layers ⓔis useful in their
own way, the key to lasting success lies in the
direction of change. True behavior change occurs
when there is a shift in your identity from (C)[within
/ outside]. If your new habit is not in harmony with
your identity, it is unlikely ⓕto last.

[How to Change]
Make Your Habit an Automatic Loop
After defining your desired identity, you will want
to integrate new habits into your daily routines. It
is worth noting here (A)[what / that] any lasting
habits ⓐ______________________________. To make habits
take effect almost automatically, we need to
understand the concept of the habit loop, which
consists of four steps: cue, craving, response, and
reward. The more smoothly this loop operates, the
more easily the habit is performed. The following
four laws offer practical guidance for each step.
The 1st Law: Cue
“Make an obvious cue for your habit.”
When creating a new habit, set a cue that sparks
the habit and make the cue as (B)[obvious /
obviously] as possible. The two most common cues
are time and location. The formula for your action
plan can be “I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in
[LOCATION].” Instead of a vague intent like “I will
work out,” (C)[being / be] specific and tell yourself “I
will work out for an hour starting at 8 p.m. at home.”
Another effective method is habit stacking. Your
current habit is already associated with a particular
time and location, so pair it with a new one by
saying something like “After I [CURRENT HABIT], I
will [NEW HABIT].” Your action plan can be “After I
finish dinner around 8 p.m., I’ll immediately change
into my workout clothes.” The more this link
between the cue and the action is repeated, the
more firmly the new habit will be rooted in your life.

윗글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: whatobviousbeing
whatobviouslybeing
thatobviousbeing
thatobviouslybe
thatobviousbe
solution: (A) 뒤에 주어 any lasting habits와 동사 take를 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. what은 선행 사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 뒤에 불완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. (B) ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’의 구조에서 목적어 the cue의 상태 를 설명하는 목적격보어가 필요하므로 형용사 obvious가 적절하다. (C) 전치사구 Instead of a vague intent like “I will work out” 뒤에 행동을 권하는 명령문이 이어지며, be와 tell이 등위접속 사 and에 의해 병렬 연결되므로 동사원형 be가 적절하다.

body:
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you (A)[want /
achieve]. The middle layer is process — what you
(B)[avoid / do]. The deepest and most fundamental
layer is identity — what you believe or who you are.
While changes in all three layers are useful in their
own way, the key to lasting success lies in the
direction of change. True behavior change occurs
when there is a shift in your identity from within. If
your new habit is not in harmony with your identity,
it is (C)[likely / unlikely] to last.

M: Hey Eliza, what’s wrong with your fingers?
W: I couldn’t stop biting my nails because I got so
nervous about my math test.
M: Oh no! Biting your nails is a bad habit. Have
you tried to stop?
W: Yes, but every time I get stressed, I start biting
them again.

nails? If you see your colorful nails or smell the
polish, you might think twice before biting
them.
W: That’s a good idea. Anyway, I really need to
figure out a way to deal with my stress without
biting my nails.

soft ball? That might help you manage your
stress.

When creating a new habit, set a cue that sparks
the habit and (A)_____________________________________.
The two most common cues are time and location.
The formula for your action plan can be “I will
[BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in [LOCATION].” Instead of a
vague intent like “I will work out,” be specific and
tell yourself “I will work out for an hour starting at

current habit is already associated with a particular
time and location, so pair it with a new one by

will [NEW HABIT].” Your action plan can be “After I
finish dinner around 8 p.m., I’ll immediately change
into my workout clothes.” (B)신호와 행동 사이의 이

ⓐA habit is an atomic routine what is easy to do
but has life-changing power. Good habits lead to
small improvements on a daily basis. Over time,
these
tiny
improvements
can
make
a
huge
difference in our lives. If you are seeking to build
and maintain good habits for a better life, here are
some valuable tips to guide you.
ⓑYou might find that challenging to develop and
maintain good habits for more than a few days.
This often happens when people focus on changing
external outcomes or behaviors rather than on
where they originate from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you achieve. The
middle layer is process — what you do. The deepest
and most fundamental layer is identity — what you
believe or who you are. While changes in all three
layers are useful in their own way, the key to lasting
success lies in the direction of change. True
behavior change occurs when there is a shift in your
identity from within. If your new habit is not in
harmony with your identity, it is unlikely to last.
You can work on changing your identity through two
steps. First, keep asking yourself, “What kind of
person do I want to become?” Once you have an
idea of the kind of person you want to be, start
reinforcing
that
identity
through
your
actions.
Specifically, repeat the action that kind of person
would choose to do, and over time, you will naturally
become such a person. For example, if you want to
start exercising daily, think of yourself as an energetic
and motivated person who cares about his or her
health. Then try to do the routines that such a person
would naturally do. Repeating these routines will
gradually lead you to become that kind of person.

윗글의 내용을 가장 잘 이해한 사람들로 짝지어진 것은?

∎ 지호: Focusing on outcomes or behaviors is
the surest way to make a habit last.
∎ 수아: A single strong action is enough to
complete a shift in your identity.
∎ 민준: To change, you should picture someone you
admire and wait until you feel ready to act.
∎ 해든: Lasting change comes from a shift in
identity that happens from within.
∎ 이도: A habit that does not fit who you
believe you are is unlikely to last.

Give Yourself a New Identity

last.

person do I want to become?” Once you have an
idea of the kind of person you want to be, start
reinforcing
that
identity
through
your
actions.

would choose ⓓto do, and over time, you will
naturally become such a person. For example, if you
want to start exercising daily, think of yourself as
an energetic and motivated person who cares about
his or her health. Then try to do the routines that
such a person would naturally do. Repeating these
routines will gradually lead you ⓔto become that
kind of person.

When creating a new habit, set a cue that sparks
the habit and make the cue as (A)[vague / obvious]
as possible. The two most common cues are time
and location. The formula for your action plan can
be “I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in [LOCATION].”
Instead of a vague intent like “I will work out,” be
(B)[specific / general] and tell yourself “I will work
out for an hour starting at 8 p.m. at home.”
Another effective method is habit stacking. Your
current habit is already associated with a particular
time and location, so pair it with a new one by
saying something like “After I [CURRENT HABIT], I
will [NEW HABIT].” Your action plan can be
“ⓐ______________________________________.”
The
more
this link between the cue and the action is
repeated, the more (C)[firmly / loosely] the new
habit will be rooted in your life.

make your habits attractive and enjoyable. This is
(B)[where / what] a strategy known as temptation
bundling comes into play. Temptation bundling works
by linking [ACTION I WANT] with [HABIT I NEED]. For
example, if you want to watch your favorite TV show
but need to work out, you can bundle these two
actions together by watching the show only while
exercising on your stationary bike in the living room.
This way, you can seamlessly do what you need to do
along with (C)[what / which] you want to do.

prefer actions that require less effort. If a habit is
easier to do, it’s more likely to be repeated. It is
important to create an environment that makes

becomes significantly easier to continue.

is readily available while keeping distractions
away. Another approach is the two-minute rule.

body:
Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual
fans but also to the performance of sports teams.
When a team competes in their home stadium, their
fans gather to watch the game. Typically, the cheers
from the home team’s fans are louder than those
from the visiting team’s supporters. This dynamic has
an impact on the performance of the home team, as
confirmed by a study in 2021.
The study examined the relationship between
cheering and goals scored in matches. It compared
home matches in an Italian football league from
2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic
when crowds were banned from entering stadiums.
It was found that the home team’s performance
decreased by eight percent on average without
crowds. This means that cheering helps the team’s
performance to some extent, although it may not
be the determining factor.

optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected

group and feel a sense of belonging to that group,
being a fan of a sports team is different from just
having friends. Optimal distinctiveness theory states
that everyone has a need for inclusion and

feel unique because your team’s fans are different
from the fans of other teams. This feeling of
uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate
use of their team colors and songs.

Another explanation for sports fandom is a
phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.” This
means that you feel successful by associating
yourself with others’ success, especially when you
are ⓐconnected to them in some way. This
phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for
their sports teams. People feel ⓑproud when their
team wins the game or performs well. Even though
a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any
ⓒimmediate benefits, the mere act of watching the
game brings them satisfaction. This connection with
sports teams can sometimes grow so ⓓstrong
among some passionate supporters that they even
identify themselves with their teams. Because of this
identification, they often consider criticism toward
their team as a personal attack and become
ⓔobedient in extreme cases.

A notable example of blue carbon can be found
in tidal flats located around the ocean. Research
conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in
Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of
carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon

offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by

carbon has become a promising and sustainable
solution to the current environmental problem.

capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having
them officially recognized as blue carbon.

Email is one of the most widely ⓐused forms of
communication today. Did you know that the
seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or
ⓑchecking
your
inbox
has
an
environmental
impact?
In
reality,
email
travels
through
an
energy-consuming network, ⓒcontributing to climate
change on our planet. Storing countless email
messages in data centers ⓓcreate carbon emissions.
These data centers rely on huge servers to store
and access data at all times. Because the centers
use electricity to run the servers and to cool down
the large amounts of heat ⓔthat they generate,
they consume a significant amount of fossil fuels.
Mike Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author
of How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of
Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For
example, a short phone-to-phone email has a
carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a
long email, which takes about ten minutes to write
and three minutes to read on a computer, has a
footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So, something as
simple as deleting unnecessary email messages can
help to save the Earth.

of ~ atmosphere)의 핵심이 단수인 One이 므로 단수동사로 수일치한 is를 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 명 사적 용법의 to부정사를 사용해 보어 자리에 to부정사인 to use를 쓴다. 이어서 목적어로 the “good” carbon과 이를 수식하는 전치사구 on Earth를 연결해 문장을 완성 한다. 13) ②: ⓑ leads → leading (완전한 절(It ~ effect) 뒤에 접속 사 없이 동사구가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문을 이끄는 분사 형태가 되어 야 하며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용이 원인이 되어 지구 온난화와 기후 변화로 ‘이어지는’ 주체이고, ‘lead to ~(~로 이어지다)’의 lead는 자동사이므로, 능동을 나 타내는 현재분사 leading으로 고친다. 참고로, 자동사는 수동태나 수동을 나타내는 과거분사로 쓸 수 없다.) 오답 ⓓ ‘비교급+than’ 표현에 의해 The carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems와 비교되는 표현이 than 뒤에 이어져야 하므로, 단수명사구 the carbon absorption rate를 대신하는 단수대명사 that은 알맞다. 14) maintain, absorbing, cost-effective, more 요약문  지구의 탄소는 온실 효과의 요인이 되는 검은 탄 소, 이산화탄소를 흡수함으로써 생태계를 유지하는 데 도움 이 되는 녹색 탄소, 그리고 대양에 저장되어 있으며 육지의 숲보다 훨씬 더 많은 탄소를 저장해 대기의 탄소를 줄이는 데 있어 매우 비용 효율적인 청색 탄소로 구성되어 있다. 15) ④: 갯벌에 탄소를 저장하는 수많은 유기체와 해양 동물이 있다는 것을 고려할 때 청색 탄소의 그 보고는 현재 환경 문제에 대한 유망하고 지속 가능한 해결책이 되 었다고 했으므로, ④ ‘갯벌은 살아있는 유기체가 없기 때문에 현대의 환경 문제에 대한 신뢰할 수 있거나 장 기적인 해답이 될 수 있다.’는 일부 일치하지 않는 내용 이다. 오답 ① 해안 지역의 갯벌은 청색 탄소의 주목할 만한 사례 의 역할을 한다. ② 2021년의 한 연구는 한국의 갯벌이 약 1,300만 톤 의 탄소를 보유하고 연간 26만 톤이 넘는 이산화탄소 를 흡수한다는 것을 보여주었다. ③ 갯벌의 수용력은 그것이 11만 대의 차량에 의해 생 성되는 연간 이산화탄소 배출량을 상쇄할 수 있게 해 준다. ⑤ 전 세계 연구자들은 갯벌이 청색 탄소로 공식적으 로 승인될 수 있도록 그 잠재력을 계속 연구하고 있다. 16) further efforts to restore getbol, we would fail to preserve this valuable ecosystem for future generations : ⦁<조건>에 따라 가정법을 사용하되, 맨 앞에 Without이 제시되어 있으며, 내용상 현재 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, ‘~가 없다면, …할 것이다’라는 뜻의 ‘Without+명 사(구), 주어+조동사의 과거형+동사원형 ~’ 형태의 가정 법 과거 구문을 사용한다. ⦁Without의 목적어 자리에 명사구 further efforts를 쓰 고, <조건>에 따라 형용사적 용법의 to부정사를 사용해 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 to부정사구가 이어지도록 한다. 즉, 동사 restore를 to부정사인 to restore로 변형하고, 목 적어로 getbol을 쓴다. ⦁주절의 주어로 we를 쓰고 조동사 will을 과거형인 would로 변형한 뒤, 동사원형 fail을 쓴다. ‘~하는 데 실패 하다’라는 뜻의 ‘fail+to부정사’를 사용해 fail 뒤에 preserve를 to부정사인 to preserve로 변형하고, 목적어로 명사구 this valuable ecosystem을 쓴다. 이어서 전치사 for(~을 위해)를 사용해 전치사구 for future generations 를 써서 문장을 완성한다. 17) ②: (A) 온실가스 배출이 대기 중의 탄소 증가로 이어졌듯 이 욕조 안의 수위가 상승할 것이라는 내용이 이어지므 로, 우리가 수도꼭지를 계속 틀어 놓는다고 전제하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘keep A -ing(A가 계속 – 하게 하다)’ 표현을 이루는 keep이 알맞다. stop A -ing A가 -하는 것을 멈추게 하다 (B) such as(~와 같은) 뒤에 기후 변화(climate change) 가 예로 이어지므로, 탄소 수준의 상승이 이미 부정적 인 환경적 결과를 가져왔다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따 라서 negative(부정적인)가 알맞다. positive 긍정적인 (C) 우리가 탄소 배출을 충분히 줄이지 않는다는 가정 에 대한 결과로 이어지므로, 대기 중의 탄소가 계속해 서 축적될 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 accumulate(축적되다)가 알맞다. decrease 줄어들다 18) ④: ⓓ create → creates (동명사구인 주어 ‘Storing ~ centers’ 에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 문장의 내용이 일반적인 사실을 나타내므로 현재시제가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 동명사(구) 주어는 단수 취급하므로 수일치를 위해 복수 동사 create를 단수동사 creates로 고친다.) 오답 ⓑ 전치사 of의 첫 번째 목적어 자리에 온 동명사구 looking through emails와 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬 로 연결되어야 하므로, 동명사구를 이끄는 동명사 checking은 알맞다. 19) ④: 데이터 센터는 서버를 가동하고 그들이 발생시키는 많 은 양의 열을 식히기 위해 전기를 사용하기 때문에 상 당한 양의 화석 연료를 소비한다고 했으므로, ④ ‘데이 터 센터는 서버에 의해 생성되는 막대한 열을 식히기 위해 전적으로 재생 가능 에너지로만 운영된다.’는 일부 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 받은 편지함을 확인하거나 메시지를 읽는 것은 해 롭지 않은 것처럼 보일 수 있지만, 실제로는 환경에 영 향을 미친다. ② 데이터 센터는 셀 수 없이 많은 이메일을 계속 보 관하기 때문에 탄소 배출을 발생시킨다. ③ 대규모 서버는 데이터를 항상 접근할 수 있고 준비 된 상태로 유지하기 위해 지속적인 전력이 필요하다. ⑤ 모바일 기기 간에 보내지는 짧은 이메일은 컴퓨터 에서 써지고 읽히는 긴 이메일보다 훨씬 더 적은 이산 화탄소를 배출한다. 20) ④: 농사와 도시화를 위한 갯벌 매립은 갯벌 지역의 감소 및 생물 다양성의 손실로 이어졌으며 추가 손실을 막 기 위해 정부와 환경 단체가 갯벌 보호를 위한 노력을 기울여 왔고, 미래 세대를 위해 갯벌을 복원하고 보존 하는 추가적인 노력을 지속적으로 기울여야 한다는 내 용이므로, ④ ‘미래 세대를 위해서, 우리는 갯벌을 복원 하고 보존하기 위한 지속적인 노력을 기울여야 한다.’ 가 글의 요지로 알맞다. 오답 ① 갯벌은 가치 없는 땅으로 잘못 여겨져 왔다. ② 갯벌 지역의 감소는 되돌릴 수 없는 생물 다양성 손실을 초래했다. ③ 농업과 도시화를 위한 갯벌 매립은 한국으로서는 불가피한 선택이었다. ⑤ 정부와 환경 단체 간의 협력은 갯벌을 보호하는 데 필수적이다.

B: Hello, I’m Jongwon. I emailed you about an interview.
W: Oh, welcome to One Earth Zero Waste Store.
Please have a seat.
B: I read an article about your store on the internet.
Can I ask you what made you start a zero-waste
store?
W: I wanted to join the zero-waste movement after
seeing a documentary about plastic pollution.
B: Great! Can you tell me more about your store?
W: My store sells organic food and household items,
including shampoo and soap. But we don’t provide
any packaging or plastic bags. Customers have
to bring their own containers to buy the
products here.
B: Wow, that sounds like a great way to reduce
plastic waste.
W: Fortunately, a lot of other people also think it’s
a good idea and visit my store, too.
B: (A)In my opinion, we need more stores that
participate in the zero-waste movement for our
environment.
W: You’re right. If we care more about the environment,
there’s always something we can do for it.
B: I agree. Thank you for your time.

I think we need more stores that participate inthe zero-waste movement for our environment.
